steps.title: Fix larvae in TCA
steps.instruction: Fix 5‑days‑post‑fertilization zebrafish larvae in 2 % trichloroacetic acid (TCA) solution for 3 h at room temperature (RT) on a rocker.

steps.title: Wash fixed larvae
steps.instruction: Remove the TCA solution and wash the larvae three times with 1× PBS on a rocker.

steps.title: Dissect brain
steps.instruction: Pin each larva to a Sylgard‑coated dish, remove eyes, skin over the head, and notochord with forceps, cut at the yolk sac to detach the head, and place the dissected brain into a 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 350 µL blocking solution.

steps.title: Block tissue
steps.instruction: Incubate the dissected brains in blocking solution for 3 h at RT on a rocker (protect from light).

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Remove blocking solution, add primary antibody diluted in 300 µL blocking solution, and incubate overnight at RT on a rocker.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Rinse samples with 0.5 % PBS‑Trx three times, then wash sequentially for 10 min, 15 min, and 30 min with fresh 0.5 % PBS‑Trx (each on a rocker).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add secondary antibody diluted in 300 µL blocking solution, incubate 4 h at RT in the dark on a rocker.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Rinse with 1× PBS three times, then wash four times for 15 min each with 1× PBS on a rocker.

steps.title: Anchor tissue with AcX
steps.instruction: Place each stained brain into a 24‑well plate, add 200 µL anchoring solution (2 µL 1 % AcX stock diluted 1:100 in 198 µL 1× PBS) per well, and shake overnight (≥16 h) at RT, 40–70 rpm, protected from light.

steps.title: Wash anchored samples
steps.instruction: Remove anchoring solution and wash each sample with 200 µL 1× PBS on a shaker at 40–70 rpm for 10 min at RT; repeat twice.

steps.title: Prepare coverslip wells
steps.instruction: Construct custom wells: on a microscope slide place two 22 × 22 mm coverslips at the ends, add ~2 µL water to adhere, then place a second set of coverslips over them using super glue; make one well per sample.

steps.title: First monomer + 4‑HT incubation
steps.instruction: Add 376 µL monomer solution to each well, then add 8 µL 0.5 % 4‑HT stock solution, and rock on a shaker (40–70 rpm) for 10 min at RT to mix and diffuse into the sample.

steps.title: Second monomer + 4‑HT incubation
steps.instruction: Remove the previous solution, add fresh 376 µL monomer solution plus 8 µL 0.5 % 4‑HT stock, and rock for 5 min at RT (40–70 rpm).

steps.title: Add polymerization initiators
steps.instruction: Add 8 µL 10 % TEMED stock solution, rock 1 min at RT (40–70 rpm); then add 8 µL 10 % APS stock solution, rock 30 s at RT (40–70 rpm).

steps.title: Mount samples for gel formation
steps.instruction: Using a glass Pasteur pipette, transfer ~100 µL of the gelling solution with each sample into the prepared coverslip well, orient the brain dorsal or ventral side up, place a 24 × 50 mm coverslip on top, and avoid air bubbles.

steps.title: Controlled polymerization
steps.instruction: Place the slides in a slide mailer and incubate 50 min at 4 °C, then move to a 37 °C incubator for 2 h to complete gel formation.

steps.title: Prepare proteinase K solution
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, mix 3.3 µL Proteinase K (>600 U/mL) with 246.7 µL digestion buffer to make 250 µL of 8 U/mL Proteinase K solution (one tube per sample).

steps.title: Remove coverslips and cut gel
steps.instruction: After polymerization, remove both 22 × 22 mm and 24 × 50 mm coverslips under a dissecting microscope, moisten the gel surface with digestion buffer using a paintbrush, and cut the surrounding gel with a scalpel, making an asymmetrical cut to mark orientation.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Transfer each gel piece into its Proteinase K tube, incubate overnight (≈12 h) in a water bath at 50 °C.

steps.title: Water washes for expansion
steps.instruction: Transfer gels to a 6‑well plate (one per well) using a paintbrush, remove residual digestion buffer, then wash with 5 mL cell‑culture‑grade water for 30 min on a shaker; repeat three additional 30 min water washes (total four 30‑min washes).

steps.title: Prepare microscope slides
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood, clean each slide twice with 50 µL water (dry with Kimwipes), then twice with 50 µL 70 % ethanol (dry), apply 50 µL 1 mg/mL Poly‑D‑Lysine to the center, incubate 30 min at RT, remove excess, wash three times with 50 µL water, and let dry. Mark the Poly‑D‑Lysine spot as the mounting reference.

steps.title: Mount gel for imaging
steps.instruction: After the final water wash, carefully remove all water from the well (dry with a Kimwipe without touching the gel), place a 22 × 22 mm coverslip in the well, slide the gel onto the coverslip with a paintbrush (ventral side up), then using forceps lift the coverslip‑gel assembly and transfer the gel onto the Poly‑D‑Lysine‑coated slide.

steps.title: Locate and image Mauthner cell
steps.instruction: Place a ~3 mm × 3 mm Kimwipe piece on top of the gel near the hindbrain as a reference, locate the brain with a dissecting scope, remove the Kimwipe, add ~1 mL water to keep the gel hydrated, view with a 10× objective (transmitted light) to find the Kimwipe spot, then switch to a 40× water‑immersion objective to locate the lateral dendrite of the Mauthner cell and acquire images.
